language_change_for_udhr: norm-defaults@0 lets a norm candidate keep the source's scope in a guard and leave every other case UNDECIDED instead of declaring allow or deny; it moved the norm candidates of u017, u052, u112, u114 and re-expressed u035, u051, u077 (the units the 2026-10-01T1800Z audit rejected) as companion norm readings with checked scope. It cannot be combined with rights@0, so the 14 right-block reading sets and the u054 and u111 units are unchanged and keep their declared completions.
language_findings: force: a strict and a defeasible right candidate need different base predicates (the defeasible one adds its exception decision), so a reading set cannot hold both and no single checked situation separates them; force is therefore fixed strict for units without a weakening word, and the 43 'shall' and Articles 22-27 units stay UNFORMALISED

act phrases: at most 80 bytes, plain words only, no 'and', 'or', 'for', 'no', 'not', 'is', 'if', each slot once; lists are worded with 'as well as' and long clauses are shortened, with the full clause in the predicate description

size: at most 64 regulated predicates per environment; four readings per right (two polarities, two bearers) cost two predicates per right once the two bearer readings share predicates through an is_state guard

reading-set candidates must be whole right blocks: 'this right includes ...' (right_lines), limitations and bars cannot be candidates, so u067, u068, u071a, u071b stay blocked and Article 30's bar is not used

limitation and bar act on rights lines fixed in the document; here every line is a reading-set candidate, so the u111 limitation has empty scope (limitation_terms 0) until per-choice elaboration exists
document reading sets cannot hold norm content, so u017, u052, u112, u114 keep companion documents for their norm candidates
load time: validating 14 right reading sets takes about 35 seconds per document load

norm-defaults@0 cannot be enabled together with soft-norms@0 or rights@0 (UnsupportedProfile: norm-defaults@0 documents on the soft and rights routes await the Lean route): the 14 right-block reading sets keep their declared 'deny' completions ('not required'), u074 keeps 'allow' in the main document, and the defeasible candidate of u017 keeps 'deny'; every norm candidate that can live in a norms@0 document is a companion with the completion unspecified

predicates have at most two arguments: a duty with a bearer, a beneficiary and a case (remedy for an act, hearing in a determination) must fold one of them into a sort, so the victim of u035 and the person of u039 are not arguments

act phrases are still at most 80 bytes in norm-defaults@0 documents: u039 ('give in full equality a fair public hearing by an independent impartial tribunal in the case', 88 to 93 bytes) cannot be stated without dropping a clause
norm candidates of a reading set hold no content in the main document (they are cited by meaning id from companion documents), so the main document's premise verdict stays UNKNOWN

no_invented_permissions.claims: every claim predicate is obligation-role with completion 'deny' (= not required); no permission predicate is used for a duty, so no prohibition makes anything permitted for anyone else. The state reading is the same duty guarded by is_state: for non-states its completion is 'not required', declared and not derived from the source (witnesses.json shows the rule decides every state under both completions and that dropping it loses the conclusion)
no_invented_permissions.liberties: the seven liberty predicates are permission-role with completion 'deny' (the tool requires some completion); in the liberty reading the rule is unconditional over the whole person sort, so the completion is never consulted (witnesses.json, both completions); in the other readings the predicate is mentioned by no rule. This stray declaration is flagged for the audit
